lesson: Always invoke the required audio-mixing and ducking tools to actually process and render the output; an empty tool-call list means no mixing, ducking, or volume changes are applied no matter what the instruction specifies.

After transcribing dialogue to derive subtitle text and timing, always complete the pipeline by generating the subtitle file and actually applying it to the video rather than stopping at the transcription step.

When asked to duck background music under dialogue, implement a dynamic sidechain-compression or volume-automation effect keyed to speech detection, rather than simply setting a single static volume on the music track.

After transcribing audio, you must actually create the timed subtitle entries (e.g., write an .srt file or add captions) using the transcription output—repeating the transcribe call does not produce subtitles; proceed to the generation step.

When applying audio ducking, derive the window (or segment) count from the actual number of speech-and-silence regions identified in the transcription rather than using an arbitrary small number, so that ducking aligns precisely with real dialogue boundaries and full volume is restored during genuine silence.
Always call add_to_timeline before render to ensure the timeline is populated, and avoid repeating the same tool call with identical parameters multiple times.
